### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/service-automation`, `@objectstack/spec`, touching **6** documentable anchor(s).

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via validateScreenInputs (symbol, a top-level function))_

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **64** of **227** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **163** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **163**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **104** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **171** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 95df345953650b225027192d5c5e4ac3c5a13bdd` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `87245ee89ef6265a2a9fdc3b5743e1867b72285f` — the merge of head `4d1aeaf3f5585b42e6b7af9583f8a7f75700b817` into base `95df345953650b225027192d5c5e4ac3c5a13bdd`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 87245ee89ef6265a2a9fdc3b5743e1867b72285f && git checkout 87245ee89ef6265a2a9fdc3b5743e1867b72285f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 95df345953650b225027192d5c5e4ac3c5a13bdd 4d1aeaf3f5585b42e6b7af9583f8a7f75700b817 && git checkout -B drift-repro 95df345953650b225027192d5c5e4ac3c5a13bdd && git merge --no-ff 4d1aeaf3f5585b42e6b7af9583f8a7f75700b817

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 95df345953650b225027192d5c5e4ac3c5a13bdd
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 95df345953650b225027192d5c5e4ac3c5a13bdd` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `dd3502f638513df86e7692ea011b5822539c575b`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/services/service-automation/src/screen-input-contract.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/screen-input-contract.test.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/screen-string-field-resume.test.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/screen-headless-caller-signal.test.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/screen-headless-provenance-durable-resume.test.ts + packages/services/service-automation/src/run-resume.ts (the gate at l.1579, the claim at l.1697), packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts (`refuseInvalidScreenInput`, l.7479), packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/screen-nodes.ts (the headless verdict's two call sites, l.449 and l.537), packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts (`ScreenFieldSpec`), packages/spec/src/automation/builtin-node-config.zod.ts (`ScreenFieldConfigSchema.type`), ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/ScreenView.tsx (what the console posts), content/docs/automation/flows.mdx, content/docs/references/automation/builtin-node-config.mdx, docs/adr/0087-metadata-protocol-upgrade-contract.md — all read in the cited code, none reviewed. The changeset `.changeset/31491-screen-string-value-domains.md` is the prose face and is judged under ② only.

Inputs: card #31491 body and all eight comments (ruling A+ in 6721960676), PR #31568 body and file list, the net diff `origin/main...dd3502f6` (6 files, +236/−9), and the 58 check-runs on the head. The head's gates are the verdicts: every non-skipped run `success`; the one `cancelled` Check Changeset run is a superseded duplicate beside two successes, not a verdict.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The resume door's accept set narrows, and only there.** `text`, `textarea`, `email`, `url` and `phone` join `SCREEN_FIELD_VALUE_DOMAINS` on one predicate, `isString` (`typeof value === 'string'`), each with `expected: 'a string'`. A present value of another JSON type under one of them is one `invalid_type` issue, `Screen field "NAME" must be a string`, and nothing else moves in the validator. **Right**, and exactly the ruling's five members on one predicate.
2. **The refusal lands before the pause is spent.** Read in `run-resume.ts`: `refuseInvalidScreenInput` runs at l.1579, before `applyResumeSignal` (l.1584), before `resolveDecisionSegmentContext`, and before `claimAdvance` at l.1697 and `forgetSuspendedRun` after it. A refused bag therefore changes nothing: the run stays paused, the #13937 shape-4 order is untouched, and the new engine test pins `hasSuspendedRun` true after an object and a number, then a string completing the run. **Right.**
3. **Shape only.** `isPresent` already excludes `undefined`, `null`, `''` and a whitespace-only string before the domain pass, so an absent value stays `required`'s question (pinned: a missing required text field yields `required` alone). A hidden or unevaluable `visibleWhen` field is skipped as the numeric kinds are (pinned with the always-visible control beside the hidden and unevaluable readings). No format of an email, URL or phone number is judged; any string is admitted (pinned). **Right.**
4. **The headless verdict moves with the door, and that is declared.** `judgeHeadlessScreen` judges with `validateScreenInputs`, so a caller-supplied non-string under one of the five kinds now answers `satisfied: false` and the screen stays interactive — the numeric kinds' existing behaviour. The changeset and the PR say so, and a unit pin (`42` not satisfied, `'42'` satisfied) covers it. The progress classification at `screen-nodes.ts` l.449 judges with an empty Map, so every value is absent there and it is unaffected. **Right** as a consequence of the one-arbiter design; the ruling names the resume gate, and this is the same predicate read at the same seam.
5. **Console callers.** Read in `ScreenView.tsx`: `text`, `email`, `url` and `phone` render an `Input` posting `e.target.value`; `textarea` posts the textarea's string. Two console paths post a non-string under a text-kind field and are now refused: a field carrying `options` renders a `Select` that binds the option's OWN value (objectui#12075, l.640-660), so a number- or boolean-valued option on a `type: 'text'` field posts a number or boolean; and a served `defaultValue` that resolves to a non-string (a CEL envelope reading a numeric column) is seeded verbatim by `initialScreenValues` (l.291-297) and posted untouched when the user does not retype. Neither is declared by the PR; no shipped flow in `examples/`, `packages/` or `ui/` (non-test) does either. Judged in ④ (F3).
6. **No authoring surface moves.** `ScreenFieldConfigSchema` is untouched, no key is added or refused, nothing at rest changes. `Metadata-protocol: none` is **right**.
7. **No public export changes.** `isString` is module-local; `validateScreenInputs`, `judgeHeadlessScreen` and the issue vocabulary keep their signatures and codes (`invalid_type` is an existing `FieldErrorCode` member; no new `error.code`). **Right.**

### ② Semver level

- `@objectstack/service-automation: patch` — **right**. A non-protocol narrowing ships `patch` under ruling A (`check-changeset-no-major.mjs` l.3738: `no (narrowing)` with `none` beside it is `none-clean`), and the level gate greened on the head.
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` and `Metadata-protocol: none` are line-initial on both the PR body and the changeset and agree with the diff (①.1, ①.6). **Right.**
- **The BREAKING carriers are missing** (F2, should-fix). AGENTS.md, Post-Task Checklist §3: "`(narrowing)` is BREAKING … a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch` and keeps its BREAKING banner and ADR-0087 disposition." The changeset's title line has no `!` and its body has no `**BREAKING**` banner. On `main`, 74 of the 75 changesets declaring `no (narrowing)` carry the banner; the direct precedent, `.changeset/30178-numeric-screen-fields-refuse-strings.md`, carries `fix(automation)!:` and `**BREAKING** accept-set narrowing at the screen-flow resume door`. The level gate only reports that the carriers are "untouched by the level"; it does not enforce them, which is why the head is green with none. The CHANGELOG this body ships into would tell a consumer nothing broke. The dev's own report flags the symptom ("the PR title carries no '!'") without reading it as this.
- **A `@objectstack/spec` changeset is owed with F1**: the fix to the spec text is a docs-only `patch` on `@objectstack/spec`, as `.changeset/30178-screen-field-numeric-kinds-contract-text.md` did for the previous ruling.
- `adr-0087: not-required (no-migration-prescription)` — **justified**. The disposition is for a change that adds, removes, renames or re-shapes no key of an authorable schema and leaves nothing at rest to rewrite; the body carries no FROM/TO prescription, so the refusal that category inherits does not fire. What narrows is the door's accept set on a submitted value, which no migration can rewrite. Same disposition, same reasoning, as both #30178 changesets; `check-adr-0087-registration` is green on the head inside Check Changeset.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Dev deviation 1 — the two headless fixtures untyped.** Answered: **a legitimate isolation, not a hidden change.** Both files measure provenance, not shape. `screen-headless-provenance-durable-resume.test.ts` (#15812) needs a NON-PRIMITIVE colliding column, because the defect it pins is `Object.is` failing across a JSON round trip; the array is the load-bearing clause and the alternative isolation (a string column) would delete the defect from the test. `screen-headless-caller-signal.test.ts` (#19846) re-sends that same array under `callerParamKeys: ['tags']` to prove the signal overrides the inference. `type: 'text'` on those `review` fields was incidental: nothing in either file asserts on the widget. Untyped, the field is outside every value domain (untyped is pinned to take anything at l.172-177 of the unit test), so the only thing deciding the pause is the provenance verdict — the comments say so. The behaviour the untyping steps around — a headless caller posting an array for a `text` field now leaves the screen interactive instead of continuing — is declared in the changeset and pinned (`judgeHeadlessScreen` with `42`; `['a']` refused on the unit door), and a real headless caller has the MCP `resume_run` verb to answer the screen with a string.
- **Dev deviation 2 — the second commit adds the adr-0087 disposition.** Answered: right; the gate asked for it and the marker is the correct category (②).
- **Dev flag — dogfood battery not run locally.** The battery is CI's; the Dogfood Regression Gate succeeded on the head (its shards skipped by path). The "no `!`" half of that flag is F2.
- `open_questions: []` — none to answer. `security_findings: none`, `out_of_scope_findings: []` — nothing to escalate.
- Check-runs: 58 on the head, all completed; Test Core 1-8/8, Type Check (workspace / consumer / source / debt ledger), Lint (ESLint / repo gates / docs guards / CI-release-engine), Build Core, Live E2E UI, Dogfood Regression Gate, Check Changeset ×2, PR-body guards and Governed Surface Queue Guard all `success`; one duplicate Check Changeset `cancelled` (superseded, not a verdict). The gate verdicts stand.

### ④ Design judgment

**The narrowing itself, against the spec on `main`.** Does it take a declared capability away at the consumer, or make the spec's own refusal real? The downstream write already holds a text column to a string (an object is refused, a number coerced to the string it prints), so the door now refuses before the pause is spent what the write would refuse after it, and it refuses rather than coerces — the same shape as rulings A′ (#17306), #30178 and #25801, by the same closed-set mechanism ("a member joins it by ruling"), under a maintainer ruling that names exactly these five members. The design is right and B and C were rightly declined. Tried to break it: the gate precedes every consuming step (①.2); engine-built signals bypass the gate but a run parked on a `screen` never receives one; object-form and message-only screens declare no contract and are untouched; a text field with a bound and a number posted now yields `invalid_type` and still reaches the bound pass (two true issues, harmless); a run suspended before the upgrade resumes under the new predicate, which a console string answers. What the narrowing does NOT do is move the spec that declares the accept set it narrows — and that is the FAIL.

**F1 — must-fix — the published spec and docs declare the old accept set, and the PR leaves them false.**
The spec on `main` says the server re-checks FOUR members and that every other `type` is a widget hint constraining nothing; after this diff the engine enforces nine, so a client author reading the contract would ship a text-kind field whose value the door refuses. Specifically:
  - `packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts`, `ScreenFieldSpec.type` (l.373-387): "Four members are value domains the server re-checks on resume (`validateScreenInputs`): the three numeric kinds … and `'file'`". False.
  - `packages/spec/src/automation/builtin-node-config.zod.ts`, `ScreenFieldConfigSchema.type` (l.953-986): the docblock "Four members are also VALUE domains, which the resume enforces" and the `.describe(...)` string that enumerates `number`, `currency`, `percent`, `file` and `record_link` as the enforced members. That string is the published reference page `content/docs/references/automation/builtin-node-config.mdx` (l.292 and l.314, a regenerated artifact).
  - `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx` l.1366-1369: "These conditions are refused … (the value shapes of the numeric kinds `number` / `currency` / `percent` and of `type: 'file'` …)" — an exhaustive list of the `INVALID_SCREEN_INPUT` conditions that omits the string kinds; and l.811-818 describes the shape check for the numeric field only.
  The fix is the #30178 shape, in this PR: the two spec docblocks and the describe string name the five string kinds as the third value-domain group (shape only, string, no format judged); the reference page is regenerated and committed (AGENTS.md "Touched `packages/spec`? Regenerate and commit its artifacts"); `flows.mdx` names the string kinds in both passages; a `@objectstack/spec` `patch` docs changeset rides beside the service one (precedent `.changeset/30178-screen-field-numeric-kinds-contract-text.md`). Code is right; the contract is what is half-moved.

**F2 — should-fix — BREAKING carriers absent on the changeset** (②): add `!` to the title line and a `**BREAKING**` banner naming the narrowing, as the #30178 changeset does.

**F3 — should-fix — two undeclared console-reachable edges.** A text-kind field whose `options[].value` is a number or boolean (the console binds the option's own value), and a text-kind field whose served `defaultValue` resolves to a non-string (seeded and posted verbatim), now get `400 INVALID_SCREEN_INPUT` at Submit — the run stays paused and the message names the field, so this is a stuck screen, not a lost run, and both are authoring mismatches the spec does not refuse. No shipped flow does either, but the console does both by design (objectui#12075). In this PR: the changeset's caller paragraph names both edges and their remedy (option values and `defaultValue` on a string-kind field are strings). The authoring-time diagnostic (an `options[].value` / `defaultValue` shape check on string-kind fields in `ScreenFieldConfigSchema`) is a `Metadata-protocol: narrowed` change outside this card — a follow-up card, not this PR.

**F4 — nit — stale leading sentence in the engine docblock, pre-existing `missing` doc.** The `validateScreenInputs` docblock on the head still opens its shape paragraph with "a screen field's `type` is an open widget hint, so no member of it constrains a value — EXCEPT the numeric kinds" before the `file` and string paragraphs, and the value-shape pass comment at l.260-263 has one over-long line; `HeadlessScreenVerdict.missing` is documented as "Required fields with no usable bound value" while it has carried wrong-shape supplied fields since #17306 (the head updates the call-site comment, not the interface doc; `missing` is not read by `screen-nodes.ts`). Not a prose face: left as an accepted deviation or folded into F1's delta.

Implemented-by: `claude/project-thread-em4tjl`

**VERDICT: FAIL**

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `4d1aeaf3f5585b42e6b7af9583f8a7f75700b817`
Local-runs: none
Scope: packages/spec/src/automation/builtin-node-config.zod.ts, packages/spec/src/contracts/automation-service.ts + packages/services/service-automation/src/screen-input-contract.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/screen-input-contract.test.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/screen-string-field-resume.test.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/screen-headless-caller-signal.test.ts, packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/screen-headless-provenance-durable-resume.test.ts, content/docs/automation/flows.mdx, content/docs/references/automation/builtin-node-config.mdx (regenerated from the `.describe()` string), packages/services/service-automation/src/run-resume.ts (the gate before `claimAdvance`), packages/services/service-automation/src/engine.ts (`refuseInvalidScreenInput`, the one production caller of `validateScreenInputs` at l.7520), packages/services/service-automation/src/builtin/screen-nodes.ts (the headless verdict's call sites), packages/spec/src/api/automation-api.zod.ts (the wire spelling of `ScreenFieldSpec`, l.233-237), ui/packages/app-shell/src/views/ScreenView.tsx (`initialScreenValues` l.293-300, the option `Select` l.640-662), docs/adr/0087-metadata-protocol-upgrade-contract.md — the two `hits` are the schema face `--paths` reads off the head's file list (the delta commit moved `packages/spec`); the narrowing floor from round 1 is kept whole beneath them, and every cited file outside the diff is read, never reviewed. The two changesets `.changeset/31491-screen-string-value-domains.md` and `.changeset/31491-screen-field-string-kinds-contract-text.md` are the prose faces, judged under ② only.
Delta-of: 6723711711

Inputs: card #31491 body and all eight comments (ruling A+ in 6721960676, the claim amendment 6723716161 widening the file surface to prose only), PR #31568 body and its eleven-path file list, the net diff `6f9f0086...4d1aeaf3` (11 files, +293/−26) and the delta `dd3502f6..4d1aeaf3` (7 files, +59/−19), and the 69 check-runs on the head. Round 1 (`record-r1.md`, posted as 6723711711) is the one earlier file read.

### ① Derived judgments

1. **The delta commit moves no code.** Read hunk by hunk: `screen-input-contract.ts` changes eleven ` * ` lines of the `validateScreenInputs` docblock and nothing outside a comment; `automation-service.ts` changes a TSDoc block only; `builtin-node-config.zod.ts` changes a TSDoc block and the `type` key's `.describe()` string — the one non-comment line, and it is the string the reference page is generated from, not a shape, key or refinement (`z.string().optional()` is untouched). No test moves. The review scope of round 1 therefore stands; the two spec files join it as `hits` because the tree now touches `packages/spec`, and what they carry is prose. **Right** — the amendment's "⛔ no accept set, schema shape or export in `packages/spec` moves" held.
2. **The accept set the code enforces is the one the prose now declares, and only that.** `SCREEN_FIELD_VALUE_DOMAINS` at the head holds exactly nine members — `number`, `currency`, `percent` (`isFiniteNumber`), `file` (`isFileIdToken`), `text`, `textarea`, `email`, `url`, `phone` (`isString`, `typeof value === 'string'`). The spec docblocks say "Nine members" and name those nine; `record_link` is kept apart as the member that takes no value, in the code (its own pass, `invalid_value`) and in both docblocks. No prose names a member outside the map, and no prose claims a format check — every passage says shape only, the format of an email, URL or phone number not judged. **Right**, and the count is exact.
3. **"Never coerced" and "the run stays paused" are both true in the cited code.** `isString` admits no number; the refusal is `refuseInvalidScreenInput` in `run-resume.ts` ahead of `applyResumeSignal`, `resolveDecisionSegmentContext` and `claimAdvance`, unchanged since round 1 (①.2 there). The new sentence in all three spec/doc passages, "a refused value leaves the run paused, so a corrected resume continues it", is what the engine pin `screen-string-field-resume.test.ts` holds (`hasSuspendedRun` true after the refusal, the string resume completing). **Right.**
4. **The regenerated reference page is the describe string, verbatim, in both tables.** The `.describe()` concatenation at `builtin-node-config.zod.ts` l.985-991 reads `… take a finite number on resume (a numeric string is refused); \`text\`, \`textarea\`, \`email\`, \`url\` and \`phone\` take a string on resume (any other JSON type is refused, never coerced); \`file\` renders …`, and `builtin-node-config.mdx` l.292 and l.314 carry that exact text; the old string (`… refused); \`file\` renders …`) occurs nowhere in the head tree, and no other checked-in artifact carries either spelling (`gen:schema` writes the gitignored tree; `gen:openapi` has no checked-in copy of this string). `check:docs` runs inside `TypeScript Type Check`, green on the head. **Right** — AGENTS.md "Touched `packages/spec`? Regenerate and commit its artifacts" is satisfied.
5. **No public surface moves.** No export is added, removed or renamed in either spec file (`check:api-surface` inside the same green job); the wire schema `automation-api.zod.ts` l.233-237 describes `type` as a widget hint and never enumerated the enforced members, so it is not made false; `isString` stays module-local; the issue vocabulary is unchanged (`invalid_type`, an existing `FieldErrorCode`). **Right.**
6. **The headless verdict's documentation now matches its behaviour at the call site.** `judgeHeadlessScreen`'s comment (l.585-589) says an issue may be a wrong-shape value "for a value-domain kind (a numeric, `file` or, since #31491, string field)"; the changeset's "Headless callers" bullet says the same. **Right.** `HeadlessScreenVerdict.missing`'s interface doc (l.368) still reads "Required fields with no usable bound value" — see ④ N4.
7. **Metadata-protocol: none** on both changesets — **right**: `ScreenFieldConfigSchema` keeps every key, type and refinement; an author's flow that parsed before parses now; nothing at rest changes.

### ② Semver level

- **`@objectstack/service-automation: patch`** — **right** (unchanged from round 1): a non-protocol narrowing ships `patch` under ruling A (`check-changeset-no-major.mjs` l.3738, `no (narrowing)` beside `none` is `none-clean`).
- **F2 fixed.** The service changeset's title is now `fix(service-automation)!: … (#31491)` and its body opens `**BREAKING** accept-set narrowing at the screen-flow resume door (ruling A+).` — the two carriers AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist §3 keeps on a non-protocol narrowing, in the shape of the precedent `.changeset/30178-numeric-screen-fields-refuse-strings.md` (Before / Now / Unchanged / Headless / caller bullets). The level gate's own text (`none-clean` for a declared non-protocol narrowing says "the BREAKING carriers are untouched" by the level) is satisfied with them present rather than absent.
- **The new `@objectstack/spec` changeset** (`31491-screen-field-string-kinds-contract-text.md`):
  - `'@objectstack/spec': patch` — **right**: TSDoc and one describe string change, no authorable key, export or shape; `none` takes `patch`. Same level, same title shape (`docs(spec)!:`) and same body shape as the precedent `30178-screen-field-numeric-kinds-contract-text.md`.
  - `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` — **right** and a better reading than the precedent's `yes (narrowing)`: the gate defines `no` as "this PR widens no published accept set or public surface" and `yes` as "it widens one" (l.2182-2184); nothing in this PR widens, so `no` is the truthful value and the arm carries the breaking signal. It agrees with the PR body's line and with the service changeset's line (the PR-body guards and Check Changeset are green on both).
  - `Metadata-protocol: none` — **right** (①.7).
